articles.title: Cyclist dead after colliding with parked trailer last week in Whitby, Ont., police say
articles.summary: A 68-year-old cyclist has died following a collision in Whitby, Ont., last week. On Friday, Durham police responded to a collision involving a male cyclist in the area of Coronation Road and Lyndebrook Road, according to a statement.

articles.title: Psychological stress in Ontario youth is down since the pandemic, suggests survey
articles.summary: The Centre for Addiction and Mental Health says psychological distress among Ontario youth appears to have decreased since the pandemic, but is still much higher than a decade ago.

articles.title: Ford to address Ontario’s economic outlook in Hamilton as U.S.–Canada trade fight intensifies
articles.summary: Premier Doug Ford will deliver economic remarks in Hamilton on Monday afternoon, a timely appearance as Canada’s trade dispute with the United States continues to escalate and provinces brace for the fallout. articles.title: Early‑morning fire engulfs Ajax townhomes; police investigating
articles.summary: A fire that tore through three townhomes in Ajax early Monday is now being treated as suspicious, Durham police say. Emergency crews were called around 5:05 a.m. to the area of Rossland Road West and Church Street North, where flames had already engulfed multiple units. articles.title: Downed tree takes out power lines near Dundas and Sherbourne; TTC streetcars diverting in area
articles.summary: Toronto Hydro crews are working in the area of Dundas Street East and Sherbourne Street after a large tree fell across the road, knocking down power lines. articles.title: Percentage of Ontario youth struggling with mental health back to pre-COVID level, survey suggests
articles.summary: The Centre for Addiction and Mental Health says psychological distress among Ontario youth appears to have decreased since the pandemic, but still remains high. articles.title: Future of Yorkville Murals festival remains unknown
articles.summary: Colourful art installations have become a beloved August tradition in Toronto’s poshest neighbourhood, but the organizers of Yorkville Murals say this could be the festival’s final year. articles.title: 26-year-old man dead after shooting involving officer in North York: Toronto police
articles.summary: Ontario's police watchdog is investigating a 26-year-old man's death following a shooting involving a police officer in North York Saturday.

articles.title: Blue Jays' Guerrero Jr. returns to lineup against Yankees following head injury
articles.summary: Toronto Blue Jays slugger Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has been reinstated from the seven-day injured list and will be active Saturday against the host New York Yankees.

articles.title: Businesses, officials praise success of car-free pilot project on Church Street
articles.summary: The pedestrianization pilot on Church Street is coming to an end Friday night with residents and officials raving about the boom in business and community vibes.

articles.title: Another Toronto street festival is being lost to funding shortfalls
articles.summary: The co-founder of the Yorkville Murals festival says they were denied city grants awarded in previous years. More applications are leading to more competition for funding, according to a City of Toronto spokesperson.
